decoder-only.d: A Transformer that uses only the “decoder” half of the 2017 model: embedding → N blocks with a causal mask → final norm → lm_head. At each position it predicts the next token. It is the shape of GLM-5.3-Flash, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and DeepSeek-V4-Flash.

fluxo-residual.d: The vector \( \mathbf h \in \mathbb R^d \) that each token carries from block to block. No sublayer replaces it: each one reads a normalized copy and adds its contribution, so the final vector is the sum of the embedding and everything the attentions and FFNs wrote.

contrato-de-forma.d: The rule that every block receives and returns a \([T \times d]\) tensor. It is what makes it possible to stack, truncate (num_hidden_layers via --hf-overrides) and read states in the middle of the stack (drafter hooks).

mixer-de-tokens.d: The block's first sublayer, the one that brings in information from other positions: full, sparse, windowed or linear attention (KDA, GDN). The second sublayer, the FFN, processes each token on its own.

ffn.d: The block's second sublayer: an MLP applied to each token separately, which opens the vector up to an intermediate width \(I\), applies a nonlinearity and closes it back down to \(d\). In all three models it is a SwiGLU, either dense or split into experts.

leitor-do-residuo.d: A matrix that receives the normalized copy of the residual stream: q_proj, k_proj, v_proj, gate_proj, up_proj and the like. In tensor parallel it is sliced along its output rows (column-parallel) and runs without communication.

pre-norm.d: Placing the norm at the sublayer's input, \( \mathbf h + F(\mathrm{Norm}(\mathbf h)) \), which leaves the residual stream unnormalized. More stable for deep networks; it requires a final norm before the lm_head.

post-norm.d: The arrangement of the 2017 Transformer: \( \mathrm{Norm}(\mathbf h + F(\mathbf h)) \). It normalizes the stream itself at every block, which gets in the way of the gradient's identity path; it has fallen out of use in LLMs.

rms-norm-eps.d: Constant added to the mean square before the square root in RMSNorm, to avoid dividing by zero. GLM 1e-5, Qwen 1e-6, DeepSeek 1e-6 (0731) and 1e-20 (Vision-Exp). It only matters when the vector is nearly null.

norma-final.d: The last RMSNorm, between the end of the block stack and the lm_head (model.norm). Required with pre-norm, because the residual stream arrives with accumulated magnitude. In Qwen it is replaced by the hyper_connection_mixer; in DeepSeek it comes after the hc_head.

fused-add-rmsnorm.d: A kernel that adds the pending write to the residual and immediately normalizes the copy for the next sublayer, in a single pass over memory. In vLLM it shows up as hidden, residual = norm(hidden, residual).

swiglu.d: Gated FFN: \( W_{\text{down}}(\mathrm{SiLU}(W_{\text{gate}}\mathbf x)\odot W_{\text{up}}\mathbf x) \), with \(3dI\) parameters. Used in the dense FFNs, the experts and the shared expert of all three models; GLM and DeepSeek also cap the activations with swiglu_limit = 10.

swiglu-limit.d: Clamp on the SwiGLU activations: \( \mathrm{SiLU}(\min(g,L))\cdot\mathrm{clamp}(u,-L,L) \), with \(L = 10\) in GLM and DeepSeek. It bounds each intermediate neuron to ≈ 100 in absolute value. It is part of the model's math; custom kernels (EXL3, b12x) have to replicate it.

column-parallel.d: A tensor-parallel linear layer in which the outputs are split (the rows of W in PyTorch's [out, in] layout; the columns in Y = XW) among the ranks: each GPU computes a slice of the result without communication. Used in the readers (q/k/v, gate/up); the column → row-parallel pair costs a single all-reduce.

layout-saida-entrada.d: The convention of PyTorch's nn.Linear: the weight is stored as [out_features, in_features] and \( \mathbf y = \mathbf x W^\top \). That is why down_proj appears as \([d, I]\) and gate_proj as \([I, d]\) in checkpoints.

flops-por-token.d: Compute cost of one token in the forward pass: ≈ 2 × active parameters (each weight does one multiplication and one addition) plus the attention term, \(4\,h\,d_h\,n\) per layer for a context \(n\). In the classic Transformer, attention starts to dominate from \(n \approx 6d\).
